validity.recommendation: no change to existence, classification, Length, Diameter, StartYear1; see the separate spec concern on SegmentCost and the Location fill below
validity.researcher_notes: The row's own harvested citation pool (9 items from the shared Florida_Gas_Transmission_Pipeline wiki page) is generic to the whole 5,000+-mile FGT system and never names 'Phase VII' -- one item is A Barrel Full (banned outright), the EIA link is a navigation page (naturalgas/data.php), and the rest (Kinder Morgan's dead 404 project page, fractracker.org's national map, oilandgaswatch.org's system entry, a 2018 PGJ 'planned projects' PDF, a 2018 Texas Energy Report story) are all system- or unrelated-project-level. So I went to the open web for a document that actually names this specific phase, and found two independent origins that do: (1) FERC's Federal Register 'Notice of Application' for Docket No. CP06-1-000 (govinfo.gov/FR-2005-10-21/E5-5807, filed by FGT Oct. 5, 2005) states verbatim: 'in phase one FGT proposes to: (i) Construct three 36-inch diameter pipeline loops totaling 17.3 miles of pipeline in Gilchrist, Levy, and Hernando Counties, Florida... FGT proposes an in-service date of May 1, 2007 for the phase one facilities.' That is an EXACT match to GEM's LengthKnown=17.30 mi, Diameter=36 in, and StartYear1=2007 for this row. (2) Southern Union Co.'s FY2007 SEC 10-K (sec.gov, an owner-company's own audited financial disclosure, independent of the FERC docket) narrates the same project after the fact: 'The Phase VII project calls for Florida Gas to build approximately 17 miles of 36-inch diameter pipeline looping in several segments... The FERC issued an order approving the project on June 15, 2006 and construction commenced on November 6, 2006. The first phase was partially placed in service in May 2007...' This confirms the project was not just proposed but actually built and placed in service on the proposed schedule -- existence and classification (an interstate gas transmission loop, correctly typed) are solid. A companion FERC EIS Federal Register notice (govinfo.gov/FR-2006-04-14/E6-5561) and a Natural Gas Intelligence trade-press story (naturalgasintel.com, 'Florida Power and Light Anchors FGT Expansion', Feb. 2008) corroborate the schedule and confirm Phase VII's purpose: connecting FGT to Southern Natural Gas Co.'s new Cypress Pipeline near Jacksonville/Clay County FL to bring in regasified LNG from Elba Island, GA. A second NGI story ('First Phase of Southern Natural's Cypress Pipeline Enters Service', April 2008) independently confirms that interconnect existed and was live by 2008. DUPLICATE check against the 50-row US-gulf roster: no other row carries 17.3 mi / 36 in for this era; P4029 (len=483, dia=24/30/36/42, cap=820) is the later, much larger Phase VIII system expansion (see cross_row_leads), not this phase. The 10-K explicitly frames Phase VII as built 'in a first phase with the possibility of a future second phase' (15.3 mi, Levy/Hernando counties, planned May 2009 in-service per the FERC filing) -- I found no evidence that second phase was ever built as a standalone project (Southern Union's later 10-Ks jump straight to the much larger Phase VIII), so its absence from the 37-row roster as a separate PID is not itself a gap. CAVEAT: Capacity (GEM 95.00 MMcf/d) is only approximately corroborated -- the 10-K describes the whole Phase VII buildout as providing 'about 100 million cubic feet per day (MMcf/d) of additional capacity,' a ~5% variance from the sheet's more precise 95.00, and I could not find a document that states 95 MMcf/d specifically for the first phase alone (tier=medium, see fills). Opened all 9 harvested citations for this shared wiki page (1 banned/skipped, 1 dead 404, 1 navigation page, 5 read to exhaustion) plus 6 open-web primary/secondary documents (2 FERC Federal Register notices, 1 SEC 10-K, 1 Wikipedia article, 2 NGI trade-press stories, 1 FGT company designee-request PDF).

validity.recommendation: flag SegmentCost=64,000,000 USD for human review; the only independent primary source found for a dollar figure disagrees
validity.researcher_notes: GEM's SegmentCost for this row is 64,000,000 USD. The only figure I could independently verify is in Southern Union's FY2007 10-K: 'The updated estimated cost of the expansion is approximately $62 million, including AFUDC.' That is Phase VII's (first-phase) updated cost per the co-owner's own audited disclosure -- $2 million (~3%) off GEM's $64,000,000, not an exact restatement. I could not find $64 million (or $64.0 million) stated for this project in any FERC document, SEC filing, or trade-press story; the only places that number surfaces in open-web search are GEM's own wiki page and search-engine summaries that appear to be quoting it back from GEM (self-referential, not independent -- disqualified per standing rule 1). Earlier, the 2005 FERC 'Notice of Application' (docket CP06-1-000) gives a different figure again: 'The proposed project will create 160,000 MMBtu per day of additional firm Summer Season capacity. FGT estimates that the total cost of the project will be $105.52 million' -- but that is the ORIGINAL estimate for BOTH phases combined (phase one + the then-only-possible phase two), not phase one alone, so it is not directly comparable either. Per the SegmentCost rule (a cost is REFS_ADDED only when a primary source states THAT figure for THAT project scope), I am not staging a ref for the existing $64,000,000 value -- the best-sourced figure I have ($62M, phase-one-scoped, updated/actual) does not match it. Recommend Update review whether $64,000,000 should move to ~$62,000,000 (10-K) or be left with a note; I have not applied either change myself.
